claim: The TREM2 crystal structure was determined at 3.1 Å resolution.
source: We determined the crystal structure of the TREM2 ectodomain at 3.1 Å resolution
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the resolution of the crystal structure in the Results section and provides crystallographic data in Table 1 and Table 2.

claim: Nasu-Hakola disease mutations in TREM2 (Y38C, T66M, and V126G) are buried within the core of the Ig fold.
source: The side chains of mutations causing NHD (Y38, T66 and V126) are all buried within the core of the Ig fold
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1b and quantified by solvent-accessible surface calculations in Figure 1c.

claim: Alzheimer's disease risk variants in TREM2 (R47H and R62H) are located on the protein surface.
source: the side chains of verified AD risk variants (R47H and R62H) and possible AD risk variants (N68K, D87N and T96K) all lie on the protein surface
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural analysis in Figure 1b and quantified by solvent accessibility calculations in Figure 1c.

claim: The TREM2 R47H variant is associated with a risk of developing Alzheimer's disease similar to that associated with APOE4.
source: the TREM2 R47H variant is associated with a risk that is similar to that associated with APOE4, previously the only well-established risk factor for late-onset AD
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous genetic studies (Guerreiro et al., 2013b; Jonsson et al., 2013).

claim: TREM2 is an innate immune receptor expressed on dendritic cells, resident macrophages such as osteoclasts and microglia, and infiltrating cells.
source: TREM2 is an innate immune receptor expressed on dendritic cells (DCs), resident macrophages such as osteoclasts and microglia, infiltrating
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction section.

claim: The TREM2 ectodomain is a V-type Ig domain containing two disulfide bonds.
source: The TREM2 ectodomain is a V-type Ig domain containing two disulfide bonds, the canonical Ig disulfide between residues C36 and C110 (βB–βF) and an additional linkage between C51 and C60 (βC-βC')
evidence: This structural feature is directly observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Nasu-Hakola disease mutations impact TREM2 protein stability and decrease folded TREM2 surface expression.
source: Nasu-Hakola mutations impact protein stability and decrease folded TREM2 surface expression
evidence: This is demonstrated through biophysical and cellular methods including flow cytometry (Figure 2d, 2e), SEC analysis (Figure 2c), and confocal microscopy (Figure 2g).

claim: Alzheimer's disease risk variants impact binding to a TREM2 ligand.
source: Alzheimer's risk variants impact binding to a TREM2 ligand
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell-binding assays using TREM2 tetramers and monomeric TREM2 (Figure 4k, 4l, Figure 4—figure supplement 2c, 2d, 2e).

claim: The Y38C mutation in TREM2 most likely disrupts correct disulfide formation.
source: Y38 is adjacent to C36, which forms an intramolecular disulfide with C110, so the Y38C mutation most likely disrupts correct disulfide formation
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The T66M mutation would sterically disrupt protein packing and probably destabilize the protein.
source: The T66M mutation would sterically disrupt this packing and probably destabilize the protein
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis showing T66 is tightly packed inside the core (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).

claim: The V126G mutation would disrupt hydrophobic core packing and probably destabilize this hydrophobic core.
source: Removal of the side chain by the V126G mutation would disrupt this packing and probably destabilize this hydrophobic core
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis showing V126 contributes to a hydrophobic core (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d).

claim: WT human TREM2 ectodomain consistently eluted as a monomer in size exclusion chromatography.
source: WT hTREM2 ectodomain consistently eluted as a monomer
evidence: This is demonstrated by gel filtration chromatography shown in Figure 2a.

claim: TREM2 NHD mutants (Y38C, T66M, and V126G) migrate as higher MW oligomers under non-reduced conditions, indicating misfolding and aberrant intermolecular disulfide bonds.
source: The NHD mutants Y38C, T66M, and V126G all migrate as higher MW oligomers under non-reduced conditions, indicating that they are misfolded and linked by aberrant intermolecular disulfide bonds
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Anti-TREM2 staining was decreased for the NHD mutants Y38C, T66M, and V126G, but not for the AD risk variants R47H, R62H, N68K, D87N, and T96K.
source: anti-TREM2 staining was decreased for the NHD mutants Y38C, T66M, and V126G, but not for the AD risk variants R47H, R62H, N68K, D87N, and T96K
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The anti-FLAG antibody showed surface expression for all TREM2 mutants.
source: the anti-FLAG antibody showed surface expression for all TREM2 mutants
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The NHD mutant Y38C displayed diffuse intracellular accumulation in permeabilized cells, in comparison to WT and R47H which displayed a distinct punctate staining pattern.
source: the NHD mutant Y38C displayed diffuse intracellular accumulation, in comparison to WT and R47H which displayed a distinct punctate staining pattern
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy shown in Figure 2g.

claim: Significant amounts of SDS-resistant aggregates were found when expressing the full-length TREM2 NHD mutants in 293T cells.
source: we found significant amounts of SDS-resistant aggregates by anti-FLAG immunoblotting when expressing the full-length TREM2 NHD mutants in 293T cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 2h.

claim: Both the Y38C and R47H variants have some signaling potential, but neither sustains signaling as efficiently as WT TREM2.
source: while both the Y38C and R47H variants have some signaling potential, as assessed by phosphorylated-ERK blotting in RAW264.7 and Cos-7 cells, neither of these variants sustains signaling as efficiently as WT TREM2
evidence: This is demonstrated by phospho-ERK immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 2i and 2j.

claim: The R47H mutation has an altered CD spectrum compared to WT TREM2.
source: Ratio of CD minima at 214 nm and 233 nm reveals that R47H has an altered CD spectrum
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular dichroism spectroscopy shown in Figure 3a and 3b.

claim: Each TREM2 surface variant produced slightly lower denaturation temperatures compared to WT, with T96K having the lowest denaturation temperatures.
source: Each surface variant produced slightly lower denaturation temperatures, with R47H and R62H marginally reduced when compared to WT proteins and T96K having the lowest denaturation temperatures
evidence: This is demonstrated by differential scanning fluorimetry shown in Figure 3c.

claim: WT TREM2 and all the TREM2 variants tested showed reversible thermal denaturation.
source: WT TREM2 and all the TREM2 variants tested showed reversible thermal denaturation as they reacquired their native spectra rapidly after cooling from 90°C to 20°C
evidence: This is demonstrated by thermal denaturation CD experiments shown in Figure 3d.

claim: TREM2 did not show differences in phospholipid discrimination or in direct lipid binding between WT and AD variant TREM2 ectodomains.
source: we did not observe differences in phospholipid discrimination or in direct lipid binding between WT and AD variant TREM2 ectodomains
evidence: This is demonstrated by ELISA and liposome sedimentation assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a–c.

claim: Both human and mouse TREM2/SA-PE tetramers were able to bind Neuro2A (N2A) and THP-1 cells.
source: we found that both human and mouse TREM2/SA-PE tetramers were able to bind Neuro2A (N2A) and THP-1 cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4b–d, f, g.

claim: Overnight treatment with PMA/ionomycin dramatically decreased binding of TREM2/SA-PE tetramers to THP-1 cells.
source: overnight treatment with PMA/ionomycin dramatically decreased binding of TREM2/SA-PE tetramers to THP-1 cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4b and c.

claim: TREM2 binding is sensitive to proteinase treatment of cells prior to incubation with the staining reagent.
source: TREM2 binding is sensitive to proteinase treatment of cells prior to incubation with our staining reagent
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4d.

claim: TREM2 binding to cells is sensitive to heparinase treatment.
source: mTREM2 staining of (f) THP-1 and (g) N2A cells treated with heparinases, chondroitinases, or both
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4f and g.

claim: The AD-linked variant R47H displayed markedly diminished binding to N2A and THP-1 cells.
source: the AD-linked variant R47H displayed markedly diminished binding to N2A and THP-1 cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4k, l and Figure 4—figure supplement 2c, d, e.

claim: The potentially AD-protective T96K variant significantly increased binding to cells.
source: the potentially AD-protective T96K variant significantly increased binding
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4k, l and Figure 4—figure supplement 2c, d, e.

claim: The R62H variant reduced binding as measured in the anti-6H format, but the reduction in binding was less dramatic when measured by competition or tetramer staining.
source: The R62H variant reduced binding as measured in the anti-6H format, but the reduction in binding was less dramatic when measured by competition or tetramer staining, suggesting an intermediate decrease in affinity
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4k, l and Figure 4—figure supplement 2c, d, e.

claim: TREM2 has a large basic surface that is not present on the surface of other TREM family receptors.
source: we noticed a large basic surface that was not present on the surface of other TREM family receptors for which coordinates are available
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrostatic surface analysis shown in Figure 5a, b and comparison with other TREM family members in Figure 5d, e, f.

claim: The basic patch on TREM2 is composed of residues R47, R62, K66, R76, and R77.
source: Figure 5c shows structure-based sequence alignment with basic patch residues labeled with blue asterisks
evidence: This is inferred from the structure-based sequence alignment shown in Figure 5c where basic patch residues are marked.

claim: Mutations R76D and R77D in the basic patch reduce TREM2 binding to THP-1 cells.
source: Flow cytometry analysis of WT, R76D, and R77D hTREM2/SA-PE binding to TREM2-L on THP-1 cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5g.

claim: TREM2-deficient AD mice display fewer activated microglia.
source: TREM2-deficient AD mice display fewer activated microglia
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Wang et al., 2015; Jay et al., 2015).

claim: The absence of TREM2 prevents microglia proliferation and promotes microglia apoptosis.
source: the absence of TREM2 prevents microglia proliferation and promotes microglia apoptosis
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Wang et al., 2015; Jay et al., 2015).

claim: Microglia in TREM2-deficient AD mice displayed less activation and did not engulf Aβ plaques.
source: Microglia in TREM2-deficient AD mice displayed less activation and did not engulf Aβ plaques
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Wang et al., 2015; Jay et al., 2015).

claim: TREM2 shows only broad discrimination for anionic (PA, PG, PI, PS) over more neutral (PC, PE) lipids.
source: purified TREM2 shows only broad discrimination for anionic (PA, PG, PI, PS) over more neutral (PC, PE) lipids
evidence: This is demonstrated by phospholipid binding ELISA shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, b, c.

claim: TREM2-lipid binding is not sensitive to EDTA, unlike TIM and CD300 proteins.
source: TREM2-lipid binding is not sensitive to EDTA, unlike TIM and CD300
evidence: This is demonstrated by ELISA experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1f.

claim: TREM2 does not bind CHO 745 cells, which do not express GAGs.
source: TREM2 cell-staining tetramers do not bind CHO 745 cells, which do not express GAGs
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4e.

claim: TREM2 binding to cells seems most dependent on heparan sulfate, as treatment with heparin sulfatases removes much of the observed binding.
source: This interaction seems most dependent on heparan sulfate, as treatment with heparin sulfatases remove much of the observed binding
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4e, f, g.

claim: Y38 and V126 are conserved within the TREM family.
source: sequence analysis reveals that Y38 and V126 are conserved within the TREM family
evidence: This is demonstrated by structure-based sequence alignment shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The T66 residue is less conserved in the TREM family, but is highly conserved in TREM2 proteins across species.
source: The T66 residue is less conserved in the TREM family, but is highly conserved in TREM2 proteins across species
evidence: This is inferred from sequence analysis.

claim: The asymmetric unit contains two monomers of hTREM2 in a parallel arrangement.
source: The asymmetric unit (ASU) contains two monomers of hTREM2 in a parallel arrangement
evidence: This is demonstrated by the crystal structure shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The limited buried surface area (~400 Å2) and chemical nature of the interface suggest that the TREM2 dimer observed in the crystal would not exist in solution.
source: the limited buried surface area (~400 Å2) and chemical nature of the interface suggest that this dimer would not exist in solution
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis of the crystal packing shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: A single N-acetylglucosamine (NAG) glycan is clearly visible in the electron density at residue N79.
source: A single N-acetylglucosamine (NAG) glycan that remains after Endo Hf treatment is clearly visible in the electron density at residue N79
evidence: This is demonstrated by electron density maps shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 1g.

claim: The nine β-strands characteristic of proteins within the Ig domain class are present in TREM2.
source: The nine β-strands characteristic of proteins within this Ig domain class are present
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Two short α-helix passages are observed spanning β-sheets B–C and E–F in TREM2.
source: two short α-helix passages are observed spanning β-sheets B–C and E–F
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Homozygous mutations in TREM2 including early-stop codons, splice site mutations, and coding mutations cause Nasu-Hakola disease or frontotemporal dementia.
source: Homozygous mutations including early-stop codons, splice site mutations, the coding stalk mutations D134G and K186N, and the coding ectodomain mutations Y38C, T66M, and V126G cause either NHD, characterized by early-onset dementia, demyelination, and bone cyst lipoma, or a frontotemporal dementia variant with severe loss of brain matter but lacking the bone manifestations
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Paloneva et al., 2002, 2003; Soragna et al., 2003; Numasawa et al., 2011; Chouery et al., 2008; Guerreiro et al., 2013a, 2013c; Le Ber et al., 2014).

claim: TREM2 mutations associated with AD contribute to disease risk as heterozygous variants.
source: TREM2 mutations associated with AD contribute to disease risk as heterozygous variants
evidence: This is stated based on genetic studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The coding mutation R62H is associated with increased risk of AD in independent studies.
source: the coding mutation R62H is associated with increased risk of AD in independent studies
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Jin et al., 2014; Ridge et al., 2016).

claim: N68K and D87N have been identified in AD patients, but their risk remains uncertain because these mutations are very rare.
source: N68K and D87N have also been identified in AD patients, but because these mutations are very rare, their risk remains uncertain
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Guerreiro et al., 2013b; Jonsson et al., 2013).

claim: The mutation T96K has been linked to a decreased risk of AD, but this mutation is too rare to allow verification of this observation.
source: the mutation T96K has been linked to a decreased risk of AD, but this mutation is also too rare to allow verification of this observation
evidence: This is cited from a previous study (Jin et al., 2014).

claim: The TREM2 R47H mutation correlates with increased cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tau levels.
source: This mutation correlates with increased cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tau levels, a well-established risk factor for AD
evidence: This is cited from a previous study (Cruchaga et al., 2013).

claim: The TREM2 R47H mutation has been identified in patients who have frontal temporal dementia (FTD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
source: subsequent studies have identified this mutation in patients who have frontal temporal dementia (FTD), Parkinson's disease (PD) (Rayaprolu et al., 2013), and sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) (Cady et al., 2014)
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Rayaprolu et al., 2013; Cady et al., 2014).

claim: Microglia-specific networks, including those containing TREM2, are those most significantly dysregulated in late-onset AD.
source: A recent study of more than 1,600 late-onset AD (LOAD) and cognitively normal brains revealed that microglia-specific networks, including those containing TREM2, are those most significantly dysregulated in LOAD
evidence: This is cited from a previous study (Zhang et al., 2013).

claim: Loss of TREM2 function contributes to classic AD pathology.
source: Recent studies in AD mouse models that are deficient in TREM2 confirm that loss of TREM2 function contributes to classic AD pathology
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Jay et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015; Ulrich et al., 2014).

claim: TREM2 plays a crucial role in central nervous system (CNS) biology.
source: Recent studies in AD mouse models that are deficient in TREM2 confirm that loss of TREM2 function contributes to classic AD pathology and demonstrates a crucial role for TREM2 in central nervous system (CNS) biology
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Jay et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015; Ulrich et al., 2014).

claim: The absence of TREM2 was correlated with increased accumulation of Aβ plaques.
source: the absence of TREM2 prevents microglia proliferation and promotes microglia apoptosis, which was correlated with increased accumulation of Aβ plaques
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Wang et al., 2015; Jay et al., 2015).

claim: The absence of TREM2 impacts the density of Aβ plaques and promotes diffuse Aβ structures, which are more neurotoxic.
source: This impacts the density of Aβ plaques and promotes diffuse Aβ structures, which in turn are more neurotoxic, and contributes to the accumulation of classic AD pathology
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Wang et al., 2016; Yuan et al., 2016).

claim: TREM2 plays a crucial role in maintaining CNS homeostasis.
source: These findings highlight a crucial role for TREM2 in maintaining CNS homeostasis
evidence: This is inferred from the cited studies on TREM2-deficient AD mice.

claim: Therapies targeting the TREM2 pathway should be tailored to genetic and functional differences with patient-specific medicine approaches for neurodegenerative disorders.
source: These findings provide a guide to structural and functional differences among genetic variants of TREM2, indicating that therapies targeting the TREM2 pathway should be tailored to these genetic and functional differences with patient-specific medicine approaches for neurodegenerative disorders
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the findings of the study.

claim: TREM2 associates with adapter protein DAP12, which contains an Immuno Tyrosine Activation Motif (ITAM).
source: Schematic of TREM2 cell-surface association with adapter protein DAP12, which contains an Immuno Tyrosine Activation Motif (ITAM)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1a and is established knowledge about TREM2 signaling.

claim: Engagement of TREM2-L by the ectodomain of TREM2 induces signaling.
source: Engagement of TREM2-L by the ectodomain of TREM2 induces signaling
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1a and is established knowledge about TREM2 signaling.

claim: The structure is complete with only one N-terminal residue and four C-terminal residues not visible in the electron density.
source: The structure is complete with only one N-terminal residue and four C-terminal residues not visible in the electron density
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the crystal structure.

claim: Ramachandran statistics for the final model are 97.7% favored, 0% outliers, 2.3% allowed.
source: Ramachandran statistics are 97.7% favored, 0% outliers, 2.3% allowed
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the crystal structure quality.

claim: Molprobity score was 1.66 (100th percentile) and clashscore was 9.62 (96th percentile) for the final model.
source: Molprobity score was 1.66 (100th percentile) and clashscore was 9.62 (96th percentile) for the final model
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the crystal structure quality.

claim: The two monomers in the asymmetric unit are quite similar with a Cα RMSD of 0.65 Å.
source: these two monomers are quite similar (Cα RMSD of 0.65 Å
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: The NHD mutant proteins do retain some level of surface expression.
source: these results suggest that NHD mutant proteins do retain some level of surface expression
evidence: This is inferred from the anti-FLAG staining results shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The NHD mutant protein is misfolded or aggregated and thus is not recognized by conformation-specific TREM2 antibodies.
source: the protein is misfolded or aggregated and thus is not recognized by conformation-specific TREM2 antibodies
evidence: This is inferred from the differential staining by anti-FLAG (recognizes all) versus anti-TREM2 (recognizes folded) antibodies.

claim: The loss of sustained signaling by the disease variants may suggest that these mutant proteins have aberrant folding kinetics or cannot bind co-factors required to sustain signaling.
source: The loss of sustained signaling by the disease variants may suggest that these mutant proteins have aberrant folding kinetics (and thus are replenished more slowly at the surface than WT proteins) or cannot bind co-factors that may be required to sustain signaling
evidence: This is speculation based on the signaling data shown in Figure 2i, j.

claim: The buried residue changes linked to NHD cause misfolding and aggregation, with variable impact on surface expression.
source: these experiments demonstrate that the buried residue changes linked to NHD cause misfolding and aggregation, with variable impact on surface expression
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The AD-linked surface mutations do not severely impact the protein folding or stability of TREM2.
source: the AD risk variants lie on the surface of the protein and do not severely impact the protein folding or stability of TREM2
evidence: This is based on CD spectroscopy and thermal stability experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The R47H mutation induces a subtle change in secondary structure detectable by CD.
source: it should be noted that the R47H mutation does induce a subtle change in secondary structure detectable by CD
evidence: This is demonstrated by CD spectroscopy shown in Figure 3a, b.

claim: TREM2 interaction with GAGs in cis is likely required to orient or cluster TREM2 to mediate signaling upon stimulation by phospholipids.
source: we suggest that TREM2 interaction with GAGs in cis is likely required to orient or cluster TREM2 to mediate signaling upon stimulation by phospholipids
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that R47H binds phospholipids but does not signal in cellular assays.

claim: Phospholipids may function to orient TREM2 on the cell surface for proper presentation to GAGs and/or additional as of yet undefined protein surface receptors.
source: Alternatively, phospholipids may function to orient TREM2 on the cell surface for proper presentation to GAGs and/or additional as of yet undefined protein surface receptors
evidence: This is speculation about the role of phospholipids in TREM2 function.

claim: TREM2 does not bind phospholipids with high selectivity or using the same binding mode as other phospholipid-binding Ig domains.
source: it does not appear that TREM2 binds phospholipids with high selectivity or using the same binding mode as other phospholipid-binding Ig domains
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison with TIM and CD300 proteins shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1d, e and binding data.

claim: There is a long and narrow hydrophobic patch on the end of TREM2 most distal from the plasma membrane that is the most likely lipid-binding surface.
source: it should be noted that there is a long and narrow hydrophobic patch on the end of TREM2 most distal from the plasma membrane (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) that is the most likely lipid-binding surface
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The hydrophobic patch on TREM2 is adjacent to the basic patch, which could mediate interaction with anionic phospholipid head groups.
source: this patch is adjacent to the basic patch, which could mediate interaction with anionic phospholipid head groups
evidence: This is speculation based on structural analysis shown in Figure 6b.

claim: TREM2 binding to GAGs is required to mediate phospholipid signaling.
source: we believe this is best explained by the hypothesis that another interaction (such as TREM2 binding to GAGs, which we show here is impacted by these AD risk variants) is required to mediate phospholipid signaling
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that R47H binds phospholipids but shows diminished signaling in cellular assays.

claim: TREM2-L contains a protein component.
source: This ligand does appear to contain a protein component, as pre-treatment of cells with proteases decreases or prevents the binding of TREM2 to these cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by protease treatment experiments shown in Figure 4d.

claim: TREM2 cell-surface ligand interaction is highly GAG-mediated.
source: This interaction also appears to be highly GAG-mediated, as TREM2 cell-staining tetramers do not bind CHO 745 cells, which do not express GAGs
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with CHO 745 cells shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The AD risk variants most notably impact binding to TREM2-L.
source: As the AD risk variants most notably impact binding to TREM2-L, we reason that this interaction is involved in the pathogenesis of AD
evidence: This is inferred from the cell-binding experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: The mutations R47H and R62H deleteriously impact TREM2-L recognition.
source: we find that the mutations R47H and perhaps R62H deleteriously impact TREM2-L recognition
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell-binding experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: T96K appears to be a potential gain-of-function mutation in binding experiments.
source: T96K appears to be a potential gain-of-function mutation in our binding experiments
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell-binding experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: T96K is associated with a decreased odds ratio for the development of late-onset AD.
source: overall it is associated with a decreased odds ratio for the development of late-onset AD
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1c and cited from Jin et al., 2014.

claim: The structural and functional analysis of TREM2 variants illuminates a surface epitope that is specific to TREM2 and not conserved among other members of the TREM family.
source: the structural and functional analysis of these variants illuminates a surface epitope that is specific to TREM2, that is not conserved among the other members of the TREM family
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural comparison shown in Figure 5 and binding experiments.

claim: The functional surface on TREM2 mediates binding to a cell-surface ligand.
source: the structural and functional analysis of these variants illuminates a surface epitope that is specific to TREM2, that is not conserved among the other members of the TREM family, and that mediates binding to a cell-surface ligand
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell-binding experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: TREM2 binds lipid-loaded ApoE and this interaction facilitates uptake of Aβ loaded into lipoparticles by microglia.
source: while this manuscript was in preparation, it was reported that TREM2 binds lipid-loaded ApoE and that this interaction facilitates uptake of Aβ loaded into lipoparticles by microglia
evidence: This is cited from a recent study (Yeh et al., 2016).

claim: TREM2 AD risk variants decrease binding to ApoE.
source: This report also suggests that TREM2 AD risk variants decrease binding to ApoE
evidence: This is cited from a recent study (Yeh et al., 2016).

claim: ApoE is not the protein component of cell surface TREM2-L because it is a soluble rather than a surface-bound protein.
source: we do not suspect that ApoE is the protein component of cell surface TREM2-L because it is a soluble rather than a surface-bound protein
evidence: This is speculation based on the known properties of ApoE.

claim: TREM2 can specifically bind GAGs, utilizing the basic patch.
source: Our study demonstrates that TREM2 can specifically bind GAGs, utilizing the basic patch
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell-binding experiments with GAG-deficient cells and heparinase treatment shown in Figure 4.

claim: Other TREM-like proteins with the same overall calculated pI, but lacking the basic patch residues, do not bind GAGs.
source: other TREM-like proteins with the same overall calculated pI, but lacking the basic patch residues, do not bind GAGs
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell-binding experiments with TREML2 and TREML4 shown in Figure 4h, i.

claim: TREM2 AD risk variants affect binding to GAGs.
source: We also demonstrate that TREM2 AD risk variants affect binding to GAGs
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell-binding experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: In NHD, the mutations are homozygous and the TREM2 is either deleted or misfolded, leading to a complete loss of function.
source: In NHD, the mutations are homozygous and the TREM2 is either deleted or misfolded, leading to a complete loss of function
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the findings and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: In AD, the mutations are heterozygous and impair function but do not completely abolish it, leading to less severe and late onset neurodegenerative disease.
source: In AD, the mutations are heterozygous and impair function (but do not completely abolish it), leading to less severe and late onset neurodegenerative disease
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the findings and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: A heterozygous NHD mutant could give increased risk for AD.
source: Under this hypothesis, it should be possible that a heterozygous NHD mutant would give increased risk for AD
evidence: This is speculation based on the proposed model.

claim: There have been reports of rare AD cases containing heterozygous NHD variants, including Q33X, Y38C, and T66M.
source: Consistent with this, there have been reports of rare AD cases containing heterozygous NHD variants, including Q33X, Y38C, and T66M
evidence: This is cited from a previous study (Guerreiro et al., 2013b).

claim: Soluble TREM2 may be a survival signal in bone-marrow macrophages.
source: We have recently shown that the soluble TREM2 may be a survival signal in bone-marrow macrophages
evidence: This is cited from a previous study (Wu et al., 2015).

claim: Soluble TREM2 could play a similar survival role in the CNS.
source: soluble TREM2 could play a similar role in the CNS
evidence: This is speculation based on observations in AD mouse models.

claim: Soluble TREM2 can be detected in the CNS.
source: soluble TREM2 can be detected in the CNS
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: Some AD risk variants, but not the NHD mutant proteins, are readily detected in the CSF of patients.
source: we have shown that some AD risk variants, but not the NHD mutant proteins are readily detected in the CSF of patients
evidence: This is cited from a previous study (Piccio et al., 2016).

claim: AD risk variant proteins may retain some signaling ability and prevent more serious diseases because they are expressed and stable enough to be soluble factors.
source: Because the AD risk variant proteins are expressed and stable enough to be soluble factors, they may retain some signaling ability and prevent more serious diseases
evidence: This is speculation based on the observations of soluble TREM2 in CSF.
